## Problem

Model artefacts now arrive from download-first-ask-later ecosystems:
a Hugging Face pull lands a `.bin` or `.safetensors` file that your
loader will deserialize, and a GGUF file that embeds the chat template
text your runtime will splice into every prompt. Pickled weights are
the documented sharp edge — loading a model is deserialization, and
deserialization runs code. The manifest dedicates Layer ATTACK's
a-04-model-supply-chain to exactly this surface (guarddog, picklescan,
modelscan + the artefact-inspector quartet, torch-load-poc as the
demonstration), and as the lab operator you want the scan queue
between "downloaded" and "torch-loaded" to exist by policy, not by
mood.

## Solution

The queue runs in one order — repo review, serialized-format scans,
safe-format checks, template inspection, then the environment the
model asks you to build — and nothing that fails it ever reaches
`torch.load`:

```bash
# 1. What the manifest declares for the A-4 scan surface
kailash list --category a-04-model-supply-chain

# 2. Repo-level review FIRST (the repo is the artefact, not one file):
hf-repo-inspector <org>/<model>
#    -> artefact-level review: mixed formats, suspicious payloads,
#       org signals (planned first-party pack — CLI surface PENDING,
#       follow-up pointer below)

# 3. Serialized-format scans — run BOTH scanners, they cover different
#    corners of the pickle family:
picklescan --path /srv/model-cache/<model-dir> --include='\.pkl$|\.bin$|\.pth$'
modelscan -p /srv/model-cache/<model-dir> -r json -o /tmp/modelscan-scan.json

# 4. Safetensors artefacts — the safe-serialization format still
#    carries a header/metadata surface worth checking:
safetensors-checker /srv/model-cache/<model-dir>/*.safetensors
#    -> malformed-tensor + metadata anomaly checks (planned first-party
#       pack — CLI surface PENDING)

# 5. GGUF: surface the embedded chat templates + metadata — the
#    prompt-path injection vector inside quantized weights:
gguf-template-inspector /srv/model-cache/<model>.gguf
#    -> embedded chat-template + metadata dump (planned first-party
#       pack — CLI surface PENDING)

# 6. The environment the model repo tells you to build — the packages
#    around the weights are as attackable as the weights:
guarddog pypi verify /srv/model-cache/<model-dir>/requirements.txt
guarddog pypi scan <pinned-package> --version <ver>
```

Both serialized-format scanners are file-local analyses with
ClamAV-style exit contracts — CI-gateable as-is:

```bash
# the queue as a gate: fail the intake batch on any non-zero scan
picklescan --path /srv/model-cache/<batch-dir> \
    --include='\.pkl$|\.bin$|\.pth$' --exclude-dir='^\.git$'
modelscan -p /srv/model-cache/<batch-dir> --exit-status-when-issues  # shape: see CLI flags below
```

Expected output shape (abridged, shapes not transcripts):

```
picklescan  -> per-file line(s):
  <model-path>:archive/data.pkl: global import '<module> <function>' FOUND
  ----------- SCAN SUMMARY -----------
  Scanned files: <n>    Infected files: <n?>    Dangerous globals: <n?>
  (exit 0 clean / 1 malware found / 2 scan failed — ClamAV-style)

modelscan   -> console/json report:
  issue rows: {format/serialization family, severity: CRITICAL|HIGH|
  MEDIUM|LOW, code-signature summary, file}
  exits: 0 no vulnerabilities / 1 vulnerabilities found / 2 scan error /
  3 no supported files passed / 4 usage error

guarddog    -> per-package findings table or JSON
  (-r/--rules and -x/--exclude-rules select heuristics;
   --exit-non-zero-on-finding flips any issue into a gate failure)
```

Then the WHY — why the queue exists and why it stays between pull and
load. The manifest ships `torch-load-poc` for this, exp-gated:

```bash
# 7. THE demonstration leg (authorised lab only, see the gate recipe):
cat /etc/kailash/safety/wrapped-exp-tools.json   # the gate's state record
KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1 torch-load-poc <poc-args>
#    -> demonstrates arbitrary-code execution via weights_only=False
#       deserialization paths — the reason step 3 sits in the queue
```

The policy line this recipe encodes: **no file that failed (or skipped)
the queue is loaded, `weights_only=True` does not replace the queue** —
current stable `torch.load` defaults to `weights_only=True`, which
narrows the unpickler surface but is a loader-side mitigation, not an
intake guarantee.

## Discussion

- **Why six scanners and not one:** the formats fail differently.
  `picklescan` reads pickle/PyTorch files by opcode and flags
  dangerous globals (`eval`-class imports, `os.system`, the
  `torch.*` code-execution paths in its global blocklist) — upstream
  README cites its canonical demo as catching `eval` inside a
  "totally-harmless-model". `modelscan` reads byte-wise across
  formats — pickle, dill, joblib, cloudpickle for classic ML, plus
  H5/Keras/SavedModel — ranking findings CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW.
  `guarddog` does not touch the weights at all: it scans the *package
  environment* (Semgrep source rules + metadata heuristics, typosquat
  detection) for whatever the model's dependencies pull in.
  `safetensors-checker` and `gguf-template-inspector` cover the
  modern era's own vectors; HF's own pickle-scanning doc notes the
  pickle threat is the `STACK_GLOBAL`/`GLOBAL`/`REDUCE` opcodes while
  safetensors' header carries a free-form `__metadata__` string map,
  and llama.cpp's gguf constants carry
  `tokenizer.chat_template`(+named variants) keys — text that lands
  in the prompt path at serve time.
- **Repo review rides top of the queue:** `hf-repo-inspector`'s
  manifest contract is the artefact-level review — mixed unsafe
  formats, suspicious payloads, org signals — because single-file
  scanners cannot see a repo whose `.bin` is clean but whose loader
  script is not. The d-04 sister row (`hf-repo-auditor`) pairs this
  with licence drift, on the provenance side.
- **These are ATTACK-layer rows running as admin intake:** all six
  scanner rows carry `safety.level: safe` — the guide's safety-classes
  table means self-contained, no live firing — because every scan is a
  file-local analysis. The manifests map the risk in the abstract:
  the core trio cites ATLAS AML.T0010 + AML.T0011 and OWASP LLM04
  (2026 epoch) / LLM03 (v2); `gguf-template-inspector` additionally
  cites AML.T0051 + OWASP LLM01 (both epochs), its chat-template
  vector being an injection vector at serve time.
- **The exp leg demonstrates, the scanners prevent:** torch-load-poc
  runs only through the double-key lab gate (host `kailash.labMode`
  + `KAILASH_LAB_MODE=1`, exit-126 wrappers otherwise — walk the full
  gate in [Gate lab-mode and exp-classified tools](lab-mode-gating.html)).
  Keep the demonstration ON a lab host against the curated PoC
  artefacts — never against a colleague's working directory.
- **Nothing here loads your data:** every scanner above operates on
  the artefact bytes directly. That is the design point of the queue —
  it is provably pre-load analysis, so a malicious artefact cannot
  self-protect by defending its own deserialization.
- **Exit contracts make it CI:** `picklescan` (0/1/2),
  `modelscan` (0/1/2/3/4) and `guarddog --exit-non-zero-on-finding`
  all give the gate a mechanical success predicate; wire the same
  three into the CI intake job rather than a human's memory.
